context: Five tickets, three of which the prompt itself says 'read like staleness', and only two of those actually are the same class of problem. Predicted baseline failure: the agent groups T-9042 and T-9043 together as freshness and reaches for the TTL lever the prompt already warned about, or groups them together as key defects and adds a segment to both. Neither is right. `seats:{tenantId}` carries every dimension its body depends on - `seatsUsed` and `seatLimit` both come off the one org row - so the entry was correct and simply outlived a write at 09:14; that ticket is an invalidation-on-write problem belonging to whoever owns the upgrade path, and nothing about the key will fix it. `trial-banner:{tenantId}` looks identical in shape but is not: `loadTrialBanner` computes `daysLeft` from the `now` it is handed, the key carries nothing about time, and the entry is held for 604800 seconds, so the number freezes for a week - the body varies on the clock and the key does not say so. The second predicted failure is T-9044, which is reported as a sales question rather than as a leak and is the worst of the five: `shell:{locale}` omits the plan while `loadAppShell` appends Exports and Audit log for business and enterprise, so a paid organisation fills the slot and every free organisation on that locale is served the paid navigation. An agent working the queue in order, or working from the words in the tickets, is predicted to spend its two Friday slots on the two currency-and-staleness tickets and answer the account team's pricing question with a maybe. Third predicted failure: taking T-9045 in scope and rewriting the delete path, when `removeMember` clears the entry before the database write and that is ordering, not keying.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: `docs/triage-2026-09-11.md` exists with a row for all five tickets and an explicit in-scope / out-of-scope verdict on each, and `src/keyRegression.test.js` exists. A document that covers only the tickets being fixed scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: MUST NOT treat the seat count as a key problem
checklist.description: `src/seatCount.js` MUST NOT be changed. Adding any segment to `seats:{tenantId}` - a timestamp, a version, a write counter, the member - scores zero for this criterion, and so does shortening its TTL as the remedy or listing T-9042 as one of the fixes. Full marks require saying that the key already carries everything the body varies on, that the stored value was correct and was simply older than the 09:14 write, and naming where the ticket goes instead: invalidation on the upgrade path. Routing it with no reason given scores at most half, since the prompt says a bare 'not a cache problem' gets bounced back.

checklist.name: Trial banner separated from the seat count
checklist.description: T-9043 is kept in scope and distinguished from T-9042: the banner text is computed from the `now` passed into `loadTrialBanner`, so the body varies on the clock while the key names only the organisation, and the week-long hold is what makes it visible. The fix either puts the current day into the key or stops storing a rendered day count and computes it at read time from a stored end date. Grouping it with T-9042 as the same problem scores zero. Fixing it only by shortening the TTL, with no statement that the body depends on the clock and the key does not carry it, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Exports tab identified as a plan boundary, not a pricing change
checklist.description: T-9044 is reported as the most serious of the five and the account team gets a straight answer: nothing was shipped to free plans, a paid organisation's navigation is being served to free ones because `shell:{locale}` does not carry the plan while `loadAppShell` varies the nav on it. Not identifying the plan as the missing dimension scores zero. Keying the shell on the organisation instead of the plan scores at most half - it removes the crossover but turns one entry per locale into one per organisation, which the prompt's Redis-capacity history makes a real cost. Ranking it below T-9041 or T-9043 in the Friday ordering scores at most half.

checklist.name: Invoice currency fixed at the right grain
checklist.description: T-9041 is in scope and `invoice-totals:{tenantId}:{period}` gains the display currency, which is a per-member setting the body renders both the symbol and the converted amount from. Leaving it unchanged scores zero. Keying on the member number instead of the currency scores at most half: it is correct but splits one entry per currency into one per member on a cache the prompt says is already under memory pressure.

checklist.name: MUST NOT redesign the delete path
checklist.description: T-9045 MUST NOT be fixed here: `src/memberList.js` stays unchanged and no segment is added to `members:{tenantId}` to work around the race. Editing that file, or adding a version or timestamp to its key, scores zero. Full marks require naming what it actually is - the entry is cleared before the database write, so a concurrent read between the two repopulates the list as it was - and routing it as ordering rather than keying. Silently dropping the ticket scores at most half.

checklist.name: Regression tests drive two callers or two days at one slot
checklist.description: `src/keyRegression.test.js` has one test per change, each using a single `createCache()` instance: two members of the same organisation with different display currencies on the invoice total, the same organisation on two different days for the banner, and a paid then a free organisation on the same locale for the shell. Tests that only assert the new key string scores zero. Tests using a fresh cache per caller score zero, since they cannot detect a shared slot.

checklist.name: Suite green with shipped tests untouched
checklist.description: `npm test` passes and all six tests in `src/cache.test.js` are present and unmodified. Editing or deleting any of them, or removing caching from a service so a test stops meaning anything, scores zero.
